findings.passage: Discussing Lil Poppa, a younger rapper on the Last Lap tour who died in February 2026 ([NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/pop-culture-news/florida-rapper-lil-poppa-dies-25-rcna259758)), Rod told Sharpe, "I never really was, you know what I'm saying, interacting with the people on tour." Poppa had sought him out a few times, "and, you know, I never do that with people."
findings.problem: Context distortion that implies culpability for a suicide. In the re-pulled Club Shay Shay auto transcript (~101:45-103:30), Sharpe asks whether there were signs he missed that might have changed the outcome. Rod answers: "I never really was... interacting with the people on tour. Like it was the last lap tour when things were not going good... I was focused on fixing what were going on on the tour and stuff that I really didn't get to bond with him for real. It was two or three times where we talked and we bond, he pulled up on me. And, you know, I never do that with people. So, I felt like I was... doing a lot. And... when I look back at it, I maybe I weren't doing enough... maybe I could have did more or talk to him," and later, "it's our job to look after each other." "I never do that with people" refers to talking and bonding: Poppa was an exception, not someone he turned away. The draft cuts "we talked and we bond," his stated reason (fixing a tour that was falling apart), and his grief and self-reproach. It then places the fragment directly after "Avoided conflict can land on other people," with a link whose headline gives the cause of death. A grieving man's regret now reads as evidence that his coldness had victims, including a suicide. C63 claims the draft makes "no suggestion that Rod's distance bore on the death," but the paragraph's placement makes exactly that suggestion.
findings.acceptance_test: Either the Lil Poppa material is removed, or it appears in context: (1) he was asked whether he missed signs; (2) he says he rarely interacted with anyone on the Last Lap tour because he was trying to fix a tour that was falling apart; (3) he and Poppa talked and bonded two or three times, which he says he rarely does; (4) looking back, he fears he did not do enough. It does not follow "Avoided conflict can land on other people" or any sentence about the costs of his distance, and nothing in the article implies his conduct contributed to the death. The C63 claim and inference in evidence-edit.json reflect this reading, and the quote is flagged for audio confirmation.

findings.passage: In his own voice, he tells it differently. "If it mess up, man, I'm going to be blaming myself," he told Sharpe, "cuz I just ain't with blaming people and because at the end of the day I brought y'all in."
findings.problem: The draft invents an inconsistency. In the Club Shay Shay auto transcript (~25:30-27:05), Sharpe asks why he started Mainstay Touring. The "blaming myself" line is conditional and about the future: if his own company fails, he will blame himself because he chose the partners. In the same answer he plainly blames the Last Lap promoters: "your one, two, three, four mistakes burn it down in three, four months... I'm just a pawn to y'all... I'm stuck with the aftermath of what you guys ruined... I'm stuck cleaning up what y'all messed up." What he says publicly about the Last Lap collapse matches his countersuit. The draft presents the Mainstay remark as his account of Last Lap ("he tells it differently"), then says "nothing public closes the gap," and repeats the supposed contradiction in the conclusion ("how 'I just ain't with blaming people' squares with his countersuit"). That turns an ordinary legal defense into apparent hypocrisy. The conclusion also offers a lawsuit filed against him ("the Grizzly lawsuit arrived three weeks later") as evidence against his settled tone. Being sued is another party's act and says nothing about his state of mind.
findings.acceptance_test: The countersuit section no longer frames "blaming myself" as his account of the Last Lap tour. If the quote stays, the text says it refers to future Mainstay ventures and includes his same-interview statement blaming the Last Lap promoters (for example, "what you guys ruined"). "Nothing public closes the gap" and the conclusion's "squares with his countersuit" clause are removed or rewritten to match. The lawsuit filing is no longer used as a test of whether his calm is sincere. C37 and type_hypothesis.unexplained #2 in evidence-edit.json are updated.

findings.passage: Grizzly's production claim, from an adverse party with money at stake, also resembles his own "I like things done a certain way." That link is an inference.
findings.problem: In a live $27 million lawsuit, the author supports one side's unproven allegation with a quote from a different context. C77 records that "over creative... I like things done a certain way... I'mma call all the shot" was about business splits with labels, not tour production. The draft also omits his direct answer on the same point. According to Billboard (October 13, 2025) and its Yahoo syndication, the countersuit says Grizzly failed to "properly load his touring equipment in and out of the venues" and made "unilateral, onerous and inexplicable routing and booking decisions" that made finishing the tour "logistically impossible." The body reduces this to "blamed Grizzly's scheduling," and the FAQ to "scheduling and routing." Readers get the plaintiff's production story, backed by the author, and never see his counter-account of production. The "inference" label does not fix that imbalance.
findings.acceptance_test: The body gives his counterclaim that Grizzly's production and load-in failures and its routing and booking decisions caused the cancellations, next to Grizzly's production-scale allegation. The sentence linking Grizzly's allegation to "I like things done a certain way" is deleted. If it is kept, it states the quote's label-deal context and that his counterclaim disputes the production account. The "Why was Rod Wave's Last Lap tour cancelled?" FAQ answer also mentions his production-failure allegation.

findings.passage: The record shows music did not absorb all of it.
findings.problem: The draft treats unproven charges as evidence of temper and leaves out his own responses. Under the heading "The temper," it moves from his father's warning to "The record shows music did not absorb all of it," then lists every arrest. The list includes a May 2025 case his lawyers say arose from him being a burglary victim, a November 2025 drug and weapons booking they call profiling (possession charges say nothing about temper), a 2022 charge dismissed within weeks, and a 2021 misdemeanor whose outcome is unknown. It then says "no psychological conclusion should rest on them" but immediately concludes that "a portrait of a man who never disturbs a room would be false," which is a psychological conclusion resting on those charges. Missing responses: the same Tampa Bay Times paragraph (archive capture reopened) says he has explained the break-ins as a way to relieve financial pressure on his mother, credits the experience and his father's lessons with turning him off that path, and told Koncrete in 2018 that he deeply regrets complicating innocent people's lives (S04 has this regret at ~23:07-24:10). The Breakfast Club quote is also cut short. In the auto transcript (~14:30) he says that as an adolescent he "would express it in dangerous or ways that... put myself [in] stuff I probably couldn't get out of" before music became the outlet. So the record does not contradict him; he said it himself. Precision: the Times says "the shooting charge was dropped," while the draft says "the charge was dropped," which says nothing about what happened to the break-in charge.
findings.acceptance_test: (1) The arrests are no longer introduced as proof of temper or of anger that "music did not absorb." Any 2025 case placed near the temper discussion carries its stated defense and a sentence that it is not evidence of temper. (2) "They do mean that a portrait of a man who never disturbs a room would be false" is removed or rewritten so it does not rest on allegations. (3) His own account appears, attributed and dated: the financial-pressure explanation, the credited turnaround, the 2018 regret, and his admission that adolescent anger came out in dangerous ways. (4) "The charge was dropped" becomes "the shooting charge was dropped," with nothing unsupported about any other charge.

findings.passage: He did not address her charge that he stayed silent.
findings.problem: The draft presents an unasked question as an evasion. In the Breakfast Club auto transcript (~45:50-46:50), Charlamagne asks, "Your crowd wasn't feeling Ari. Do you... would you change that in hindsight? Would you have made a different decision?" That is a question about the booking, not about Lennox's charge that he stayed silent. His answer also includes "maybe that was like a management call," "I'm glad I worked with her. I want to work with her again," and "I had a good experience." The draft omits all of these. The paragraph's lead sentence, "Avoided conflict can land on other people," states a motive for his silence (conflict avoidance) that no source gives; it is the author's type theory presented as fact.
findings.acceptance_test: The article says what he was asked (whether he would change the booking decision) and does not suggest he dodged her silence charge. Either state that he was not asked about it, or cut the sentence. At least one of his omitted statements of goodwill or responsibility ("management call," wanting to work with her again) is included. The lead sentence no longer attributes his silence to conflict avoidance; it frames the cost as Lennox's account (for example, "Lennox's account shows how that distance can land on others").

findings.passage: Both 2025 cases were unresolved in the reporting reviewed as of September 2026.
findings.problem: The draft states criminal exposure as current without a current check. The newest reporting in the evidence record on either 2025 case is Rolling Stone, November 10, 2025. research_tasks still lists "Get the disposition of the open legal matters before publication." "As of September 2026" tells readers the case status was checked this month, and it was not. My search on 2026-09-17 found no report of a dismissal, but a lack of coverage is not a court disposition. If either case has been dropped, the article tells readers a man still faces weapons charges he no longer faces. The same weakness applies to the 2021 battery ("this research did not find the outcome") and the Grizzly FAQ. A related fairness gap: the draft names his former agent Beau Williams as allegedly receiving $1.8 million in "under-the-table" payments. The coverage reviewed (Billboard, Yahoo syndication) includes no response from Williams or AG Entertainment, and the draft does not say so.
findings.acceptance_test: Either the Fulton County dockets (and, if possible, the 2021 battery case) are checked, with the result and check date recorded in evidence-edit.json and reflected in the text, or the sentence is tied to its real date (for example, "no disposition had been reported as of the latest coverage found, from November 2025") with a review_trigger kept. The Beau Williams sentence says no response from Williams or AG Entertainment was found, or names him only as "his former agent."

findings.passage: He repeatedly takes himself out of the frame: he lets a public image he calls wrong stand, declines grievances about awards, and says he cannot talk about his feelings with people, only in songs.
findings.problem: The metadata and thesis lines claim more than he said. In the Breakfast Club auto transcript (~14:30), he says that when he couldn't talk to anyone, "I'd go around my homeboys and they understand how I feel or I get in the stu[dio]." So "only in songs" (this FAQ) and "can't tell people how he feels" (description) overstate a limit he describes as partial. The H2 answer's general "declines grievances" also conflicts with the public grievances on record: the 2021 Instagram attack on Alamo Records (S18, not used), the 2025 hiatus post ("I dont fw you"), and "what you guys ruined" about the Last Lap promoters. Likewise, "Speaking as himself, to a crowd or to one person, is the part of the job he keeps avoiding" is the author's thesis stated as fact, although the draft itself uses three long 2026 interviews and a multi-day in-person pitch to Ye's team.
findings.acceptance_test: The FAQ and description say he describes finding it hard to talk about feelings, not that he talks about them only in songs. The H2 answer narrows "declines grievances" to the awards grievance (or otherwise acknowledges his public grievances). The "keeps avoiding" sentence is framed as the article's reading (for example, "seems to be the part of the job he avoids").

findings.passage: It costs him something, he admitted: "I wish people didn't ... take my image and run with it."
findings.problem: Three truncated quotes make him sound more pained, detached or reluctant than his full answers. (1) Image: the full sentence (Breakfast Club ~9:40) is "kind of like a good a negative and a plus because negative like I wish people didn't... take my image and run with it, but it's a plus because that mysterious... make them want to dig a little deeper." Earlier he also says "I give them so so little that they got to work with what they got." He describes a mixed trade-off he partly owns, and "he admitted" turns that into a confession of cost. (2) Heartbreak (Club Shay Shay ~68:30-69:40): after "ain't nothing or nobody never yours," he adds that it "made me a better person" because "you should treat it like it's a privilege to be with somebody... your feelings matter. My feeling matter," and he pre-empts being cast as "negative nasty like they always try to make me to be." The draft keeps only the part about protecting his work, which reads as cold detachment. (3) Depression (Breakfast Club ~22:30): "Yeah, been there" is immediately followed by "But that [ __ ] not like everyday," which the draft drops after "when pressed he allowed."
findings.acceptance_test: The image passage mentions the upside he names (mystique makes people dig deeper) and his own "I give them so little" point, or drops "he admitted." The heartbreak section includes his stated relational lesson (treating a partner as a privilege whose feelings matter) or equivalent. The depression line keeps "not like everyday" or drops the "when pressed" framing. All three are flagged for audio confirmation.

"Is there anything I could have done better up there tonight? I don't really know what to say between the songs."

protected_passages.passage: That is a man about to turn 28 interpreting what happened at 17, and people often recast accidents as strategy. It still shows how he understands his distance today, as a rule he chose to keep.

assessment: Scope: fairness proxy only. I do not speak for Rod Wave. I read the frozen draft and evidence, re-pulled the Club Shay Shay and Breakfast Club auto transcripts (not audio), reopened the Tampa Bay Times archive capture, checked the countersuit coverage through Yahoo's syndication (Billboard and Vibe returned tollbit 402 redirects), and searched on 2026-09-17 for dispositions of the legal matters (none found; this does not establish that they are still pending). The draft is careful in most places. It attributes allegations, gives dispositions and his lawyers' denials, labels inferences, avoids suicide method, and states its source limits up front. The problems are concentrated where the Type 9 "strain" sections need adverse material. There, four quotes lose context in ways that hurt him: (1) grief and self-reproach about Lil Poppa become evidence that his distance has victims (blocker); (2) a forward-looking remark about Mainstay is presented as his account of Last Lap, creating a contradiction his same answer refutes; (3) an unproven plaintiff allegation gets the author's support while his counter-allegation about production is omitted; (4) a question he was never asked about Ari Lennox's silence charge is presented as evasion. The temper section also arranges unproven charges, including a case his lawyers say arose from a burglary against him, as evidence of anger, while omitting the regret and explanation reported in the same Times paragraph. Several of these repairs also weaken the case against Type 9 (he does voice grievances, and the countersuit matches his public blame), so the editor should expect the "strain" sections to shrink, not just soften. Risks: sensitive allegations (criminal charges, domestic battery, a suicide-adjacent passage, bribery allegations against a named third party), contested typing (medium confidence, 9 vs 4), and historical source uncertainty (auto-transcript speaker attribution, conflicting first-performance dates, a Lennox date inferred from "Last year") all hold, so the expanded jury is warranted. No major thesis change was introduced at this stage. Similarity advisory: the tripped Ibai-Llanos pair shares only the ordinary phrase "the Nine reading," and the Victoria-Justice and Sudeikis/Abrams matches ("insisting on," "keep the peace") are generic type vocabulary in the definitional paragraph, not reused arguments. I found no meaningful formulaic reuse relevant to fairness.
